items.title: Meta Ads: $89.26 spend, 3 leads, $29.75 CPL — Flooring Problems Campaign
items.summary: Over the widened 2026-08-14 to 2026-08-15 window (covering the gap since the last run's 2026-08-13 window), Meta spent $89.26 across the only actively-delivering campaign, Flooring Problems Campaign, generating 3 leads at $29.75 CPL. That's about 1.96x the 7-day baseline CPL (~$15.21 over $349.84 / 23 leads) — elevated but just under the 2x anomaly threshold, so not flagged. Account is ACTIVE, no ads are DISAPPROVED or WITH_ISSUES.

needs_attention: Last successful meta-ads run (2026-08-14) covered window 2026-08-13 only; that left 2026-08-14 uncovered. Widened this run to --days 2 (since=2026-08-14, until=2026-08-15) to close the gap through yesterday, well under the 7-day cap.

The 7-day baseline pull (2026-08-09 to 2026-08-15) necessarily overlaps the 2-day widened window itself (both include 2026-08-14 and 2026-08-15), so the CPL-vs-baseline comparison above is somewhat self-referential this run — treat the 1.96x figure as directional, not a clean prior-period comparison.

Flooring Problems Campaign's raw actions again show lead-like conversion types outside the script's documented LEAD_ACTION_TYPES set (offsite_complete_registration_add_meta_leads=3, offsite_search_add_meta_leads=3, offsite_content_view_add_meta_leads=3 — each matching the counted lead value of 3 exactly, same pattern as the 2026-08-14 run). Recommend extending the script's action-type set rather than continuing to hand-verify each run.
